newsitem.title: UK: British beef sales stage full recovery from BSE.
newsitem.headline: British beef sales stage full recovery from BSE.

text.p: British beef sales have staged a dramatic recovery since last year's madcow crisis, the Meat and Livestock Commission (MLC) said on Thursday.

The MLC said beef sales in the four weeks ending June 29 were up 32 percent from the same period last year, when fears of a link between Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE or madcow disease) and its human equivalent had sent sales plummeting.
Sales were up 0.6 percent from the same four weeks in 1995, before the scare.
"Consumers now recognise they can be confident in the quality of our product and have returned to buying in large numbers," Gwynn Howells of the MLC said in a statement.
Sales have been helped by the decision of two major burger chains in Britain to begin buying British beef once more, the MLC said.

British beef is still subject to a worldwide export ban, imposed by the European Union last year because of fears that people could contract a new strain of the human equivalent of madcow disease, Creutzfeldt Jacob disease, from eating beef infected with BSE.
